info.name: ProofTell API
info.description:
ProofTell checks a phone number, an email address and an IP address: one at a time, or together as a 0 to 100 risk score with a verdict and its reasons. Phone lookups come in five levels (basic, line type, current carrier, line status, fraud score); emails are verified down to the mailbox; IPs are read for Tor, VPN and datacenter use and their geography.

Version 1: new fields, endpoints and error codes may appear at any time, so ignore what you do not know; a documented endpoint or field is removed or renamed only after the notice the terms of service give (60 days, §6).

Every request but the rate card sends `Authorization: Bearer {{api_key}}`: set the collection variable `api_key`. Create a key in the ProofTell dashboard (Developers → Integrations), named after this platform (Postman). A `pt_test_` key is the free sandbox: simulated, deterministic answers. A `pt_live_` key spends the account's balance. The sandbox's documented inputs: `+447700900123` (a GB mobile), `jane@example.com` (deliverable), `203.0.113.1` (a clean US address), `203.0.113.66` (Tor); the sandbox answers 501 on the files endpoints.

`base_url` is `https://api.prooftell.com`. Money is a decimal string in USD, never a float. An error answers `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` under its HTTP status (401 `invalid_api_key`, 402 `insufficient_balance` with the amounts, 429 `rate_limited` with `retry_after`), and the test on every request fails with that code and message. The reference: https://prooftell.com/docs

item.name: Pricing and balance
item.description: The public rate card, and the balance of the account the key belongs to: 200 proves the key.

request.name: The rate card
request.description:
Public. One price list for everyone: the rate of every signal per run and per 1,000 (the list, what a
month's first 10,000 checks of a signal cost), its volume tiers — each check of a signal prices at the tier
the account's month has reached, per the curve —, country bands for banded signals, the top-up amounts, the
minimum top-up and the monthly amounts. Cached for five
minutes. The website, the dashboard and the docs all read prices from here.

request.name: Look up a phone number
request.description:
A phone lookup in five levels, each including the ones before it (`level`, default `line_type`):

- **basic** — free: whether the number is valid, its E.164, international and national formats, its country
  and calling code. No line type, no carrier.
- **line_type** — plus the line type (mobile, fixed line, VoIP, toll-free, premium-rate…), the carrier the
  range was allocated to (`original_carrier`), the region and the time zone, from the numbering plan.
  Charged when `status` is `success`; a number that could not be parsed is answered and free.
- **current_carrier** — plus the carrier the number is on today and whether it was ported
  (`current_carrier`).
- **line_status** — plus whether the subscriber is on the network right now and, when not, why —
  switched off, absent, unknown subscriber… (`line_status`, an HLR lookup; `current_carrier` is filled from
  the same network answer).
- **fraud_score** — plus the number's fraud intelligence: validity against the regulator's allocated ranges,
  the range's service type (premium-rate, satellite, VoIP, M2M…), IPRN and MSRN flags with dates, a 0–100
  score with its `risk_level` (`fraud_score`; `current_carrier` and `line_status` are filled from the same
  answer, presence without the reason detail).

Charged from your balance at the step of the volume curve your account's month has reached for each line
(`curve` on `/v1/pricing`: the list for a month's first 10,000 checks of a signal, less past them; `cost`
says what this call cost). Without balance a call fails with 402 `insufficient_balance` and the amounts to
top up — `basic` too: it costs nothing, but like every live call it needs a balance. There is no free quota;
the sandbox is the free path.

The levels above line type are provider-backed: they need balance,
are priced per country band (`/v1/pricing`), and the call's cost is the line type's line plus
the level's line, each charged on its own outcome. Where ProofTell does not offer a level —
for the number's country, or at all yet — its line says `unavailable` with `not_offered` or
`not_offered_in_country`, costs nothing, and the line type's answer still comes back. When nothing
can run, the call fails with 503.

**Line status where it reaches.** The presence check reaches some mobile networks and not others;
the dashboard's Coverage page lists them by country and carrier. In a country where it
reaches none — the United States among them — a `line_status` request is answered from the current
carrier. On a network it does not reach — or a fixed line — the presence check names the
network but not the subscriber's state. Either way the answer carries the `current_carrier` block
and a `line_status` block with `covered: false` and `reason: network_not_covered` (`fixed_line` for
a fixed line), the `line_status` line is `unavailable` with that reason and costs nothing, and the
`current_carrier` line carries the charge: the call costs line type plus current carrier, never line
status. When the check can name only the network the number was issued to, `current_carrier` has that
as `original_carrier` (no `carrier`, no `ported`) and the call costs line type only. Where the
current carrier level is not offered (for the number's country, or at all), its line is `unavailable`
with that reason, the answer carries no `current_carrier` block and no network, and the call costs
line type only.

**Fraud score without presence.** Where the fraud score cannot query presence, `line_status` comes back
with `reason: presence_not_available` and the call is charged for what came back: the
`current_carrier` line (when the carrier the number is on today is known — the United States, for
one) plus the `fraud_score` line at the rate of the score alone (`phone_fraud_score_only` on
`/v1/pricing`), the `line_status` line `unavailable` at no cost. When portability is not available either,
`current_carrier` is `unavailable` with `portability_not_available`, the network known is under
`current_carrier.original_carrier`, and the call costs line type plus the score alone — as it does when
the current carrier level is not offered for the number: then its line says so, and the answer
carries no `current_carrier` block and no network.

With a `pt_test_` key the call is a sandbox: the result is simulated and deterministic, no
signal is called, nothing is billed, and the answer carries every field a live one has. A level
your organization is not offered answers as it does with a live key: its line `unavailable` with
`not_offered`, no block. Any number works and its country follows the dialling code
(`+447700900123` is a GB mobile); a national number is read in `country`, as with a live key
(`07700 900123` with `GB` is that mobile). `+15005550001` is a valid mobile, `+15005550002` VoIP
(fraud score: medium), `+15005550003` not valid (`status: success`, `valid: false`, `reason:
unrecognized_range`), `+15005550004` answers 503 as an unavailable signal would,
`+15005550006` a premium-rate IPRN (line type: `premium_rate`; fraud score: high), `+15005550007` toll-free,
`+15005550008` a line of unknown type and `+15005550009` a ported number (current carrier: on
another carrier). The sandbox follows the coverage: a US number at `line_status` gets the
uncovered answer, as with a live key. `+447700900005` is switched off (line status: not present), and
`+447700900010` is on a network line status does not reach.
`+442079460000` is a fixed line (line status: `fixed_line`; fraud score: `presence_not_available`), and
`+447700900011` is on a network with no portability data (line status: only
`current_carrier.original_carrier`, charged as line type; fraud score: `presence_not_available`, the
`current_carrier` line `unavailable` with `portability_not_available`). At `basic` no number is
magic: the check is the api's own, computed for any number as with a live key.

response.name: Sandbox (200)

request.name: Verify an email address
request.description:
Verimail's verification, sold by ProofTell: the response is Verimail's `/v3/verify` JSON —
`status`, `result`, `verdict`, `reason`, `billed`, `suggested_action`, `flags` and the rest,
unchanged — plus ProofTell's `cost`, `currency` and `signals`. A run is charged exactly when
Verimail would have charged it (its `billed` is `true`): syntax errors, unknowns and
softbounces are free.

Same rules as `/v1/phone` when the balance cannot cover a run. `timeout` (milliseconds,
at most 45000, Verimail's own budget) bounds the SMTP dialogue; past it the address comes
back `unknown`, free.

With a `pt_test_` key the call is a sandbox, simulated and free, in Verimail's own
vocabulary — its four verdicts (`deliverable`, `undeliverable`, `risky`, `unknown`), its
`reason` names and `code`s, `billed`, `suggested_action` and `flags`. Any address is
`deliverable` (`mailbox_exists`); `<name>@sandbox.prooftell.com` with `<name>` one of
`undeliverable` (`hardbounce`, `mailbox_rejected`), `disposable` (`risky`,
`disposable_domain`), `catchall` (`risky`, `domain_catch_all`), `greylisted` (`unknown`,
`softbounce`, free), `risky` (`inbox_full`, `mailbox_full`) or `role` (deliverable, with
`flags.role_account`) gives that result; `unavailable` answers 503.

response.name: Sandbox (200)

request.name: Look up an IP address
request.description:
ProofTell's own IP intelligence: geography and network from GeoLite2, plus open Tor,
VPN and datacenter lists — all in ProofTell's infrastructure, the address never leaves.
Charged when the address parsed and was looked up; a private or reserved address is
answered (`routable: false`) and free. Same rules as `/v1/phone` when the balance cannot
cover a run.

With a `pt_test_` key the call is a sandbox, simulated and free: `203.0.113.1` is clean,
`203.0.113.66` Tor, `203.0.113.77` VPN, `203.0.113.99` datacenter and `203.0.113.4`
answers 503.

response.name: Sandbox (200)

item.name: Assess the risk of an identity

request.name: Assess the risk of an identity
request.description:
Send any mix of phone, email and IP. Each signal runs in parallel; a supplied signal that
cannot run (its source unavailable, or not offered) is reported, never guessed; one not
supplied is absent from the answer.

When a supplied signal is unavailable — its source down or past its time budget, or the signal
not offered right now (its line says `reason: not_offered`) — the score comes from the signals
that ran, the missing one adds a 0-point reason `signal_unavailable_<signal>`, and the verdict
is raised to at least `review` (an organization setting can turn the raise off). When none of
the supplied signals ran, the call fails with 503 `signals_unavailable`.

The call costs the signals that returned a result, each at the step of the volume curve your
account's month has reached for that signal (`curve` on `/v1/pricing`; `cost`, `currency`, and a
line per signal); unavailable signals cost nothing. The same rules as `/v1/phone` apply when the
balance cannot cover the call: the 402 names its whole price.

With a `pt_test_` key the call is a sandbox: results are simulated and deterministic, no
signal is called, nothing is billed, and `mode` is `test`. Any input works, and every
documented reason can be reached: phones `+15005550001` (valid mobile), `+15005550002`
(VoIP), `+15005550003` (not valid), `+15005550004` (signal unavailable), `+15005550007`
(toll-free), `+15005550008` (unknown line type), any other number with the country of its
dialling code (`+447700900123` with the US sandbox IP is a `geo_mismatch`; a national number
is read in `country`, as with a live key); emails
`<name>@sandbox.prooftell.com` with `<name>` one of `deliverable`, `undeliverable`,
`disposable`, `catchall`, `greylisted`, `risky`, `role`, `unavailable`; IPs `203.0.113.1`
(clean, US), `203.0.113.66` (Tor), `203.0.113.77` (VPN), `203.0.113.99` (datacenter),
`203.0.113.4` (unavailable).

Rate limit: 20 requests a second per key on each server instance, bursts of 50 (429
`rate_limited`): an approximate ceiling against runaway clients, not a quota — with several
instances serving, a key may get more through.

response.name: Sandbox (200)

request.name: Start a file job
request.description:
Two ways in. **Signed upload** (up to 1 GB and 5 million rows; an XLSX up to 50 MB): send JSON `{name, content_type}`; the answer carries
`upload_url` and `headers` — PUT the bytes there with exactly those headers (the URL accepts one
upload of at most 1 GB, for 12 hours), then call `finish`. **Direct upload** (up to 32 MB): send the bytes as
`multipart/form-data` field `file`; analysis runs at once and the answer is the analysed job. A request
body over 32 MB is refused with a 413 by the platform before it reaches the api, without a JSON body:
use the signed upload for larger files.
Upload and analysis are free. CSV, TSV, TXT (one value per line) and XLSX. Files need a
live key: with a `pt_test_` key every `/v1/files` call answers 501 `sandbox_not_available`.

request.name: Run the file
request.description:
Holds what the file's unique rows cost per selected signal on your balance — priced down the
volume curve from the step your account's month has reached for that signal (`curve` on
`/v1/pricing`), the dearest country bands at the dearest steps — (402 `insufficient_balance`
with the amounts when it cannot cover it), then runs. Rows are charged as they complete, at
the step each reaches, against the hold, and what is left of it is released at the end;
duplicates run once and are flagged in `pt_duplicate_of`; rows a source could not judge are
free. `columns` overrides the detected mapping (0-based; -1 = none). `country` reads the phone
column's national numbers in that country (`0612345678` with `MA`); a number written with its
country code keeps it. Without `country`, give numbers in E.164; a `country` that is not an
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code with a numbering plan is 400 `bad_request`.

The phone column runs at one level (`signals`: `phone_line_type`, or `phone_current_carrier`, `phone_line_status`
or `phone_fraud_score`; `basic` is by API only), priced as `/v1/phone` prices it: the line type's line plus
the level's at each number's country band, held with the dearest bands first. A level needs to be offered to
your organization (400 otherwise) and no disputed card payment on the account (403 `payment_disputed`);
a number no numbering plan knows runs line type only, its level line free, and a country where the
level is not served answers `not_offered_in_country` for that row, free.

item.name: Compatibility
item.description: The verify call of Veriphone and Verimail, answered by ProofTell under the same names.

item.name: Compatibility: Veriphone's and Verimail's verify call

request.name: Compatibility: Veriphone's and Verimail's verify call
request.description:
Veriphone's and Verimail's `/v3/verify`, served as they are under a ProofTell key: a caller of either moves
to ProofTell by changing the base URL and the key, nothing else. New integrations use `/v1/phone` and
`/v1/email`, which take a JSON body and the five phone levels; this call exists for the integrations written
against those two APIs, and is part of this contract (the notice above applies to it).

One call verifies one thing, chosen by the parameter sent:

- `phone` — Veriphone's call: `mode` is the level (`static`, the default, is `line_type`; `current` is
  `current_carrier`; another value is 400 `invalid_level`); `record` is read and ignored. `default_country`
  is `country`, read as Veriphone reads it: a value that is not a country with a numbering plan is ignored,
  and a national number sent without one is read in the country of the address the call comes from
  (ProofTell's own GeoLite2: the address goes nowhere). The answer is Veriphone's for that mode, field by
  field, a [CompatPhoneResult](https://prooftell.com/docs#schema-CompatPhoneResult): at `mode=current`, Veriphone's current-mode fields
  (`current_carrier` is the carrier's name, `ported`, `current_mccmnc`…), not `/v1/phone`'s
  `current_carrier` block; plus ProofTell's `cost`, `currency`, `signals` and `level`, charged as
  `/v1/phone` charges that level.
- `email` — Verimail's call: `timeout` as on `/v1/email`; `evidence` is read and ignored. The answer is
  `/v1/email`'s: Verimail's JSON plus `cost`, `currency` and `signals`.

Both at once, or neither, is 400 `bad_request`. Parameters are read from the query string first, then the
form body, as the two APIs read them; the key is `Authorization: Bearer`, or else the form field or the query
parameter `key` (never a cookie). Prefer the header and a form body. The rules of `/v1/*` apply: the rate
limits, the balance (402 `insufficient_balance`), the sandbox with a `pt_test_` key. An error comes in the
envelope those callers already parse, a [CompatError](https://prooftell.com/docs#schema-CompatError): `status` is `error`, `code` the
HTTP status, `type` ProofTell's error code and `message` the sentence.

query.description: Veriphone's call: the number, E.164, or national with `default_country`.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, for a number in national format; without it (or with a value that is not a country), the country of the address the call comes from.
Milliseconds for the SMTP dialogue, as on `/v1/email`.
The API key, when it is not sent as the bearer.
